title: Why Normalize Feature Maps?
text:
Why Normalize Feature Maps?
Problem
Deep networks may produce activations with unstable scale and distribution
across layers. This can make optimization slower or more sensitive to
initialization and learning rate.
Key idea
Normalization layers re-center and re-scale activations using statistics
computed over selected tensor axes.
Default stack
Conv →Norm →Activation →(Pool) →· · ·

title: BatchNorm2d: Train vs Eval
text:
BatchNorm2d: Train vs Eval
Training mode
• Uses mean and variance from the current mini-batch.
• Updates running mean and running variance.
Evaluation mode
• Uses stored running mean and running variance.
• Output no longer depends on other samples in the current batch.
Takeaway
With BatchNorm, model.train() and model.eval() change the behavior
of the layer.

title: LayerNorm: Two Common Interpretations
text:
LayerNorm: Two Common Interpretations
CNN-style direct use
For NCHW tensors, one may use:
nn.LayerNorm((C, H, W ))
which normalizes over all feature-map dimensions of each sample.
Transformer-style use
After reshaping feature maps into tokens:
X ∈RB×N×D
LayerNorm usually normalizes over the feature dimension D for each token.
Takeaway
LayerNorm is flexible; its behavior depends on the chosen normalized shape.

title: GroupNorm: Special Cases
text:
GroupNorm: Special Cases
General form
nn.GroupNorm(G, C)
Important special cases
• G = 1: similar to LayerNorm over C, H, W for each sample.
• G = C: similar to InstanceNorm over H, W for each sample and channel.
Takeaway
GroupNorm forms a bridge between LayerNorm-like and InstanceNorm-like
behavior.

title: When to Use Which Normalization?
text:
When to Use Which Normalization?
Rules of thumb
• BatchNorm2d: strong default for CNNs with sufficiently large batch
size.
• GroupNorm: useful when batch size is small, common in detection and
segmentation.
• LayerNorm: common in Transformers and token-based architectures.
• InstanceNorm2d: common in style transfer, image generation, and
appearance normalization.
Takeaway
The best normalization layer depends on architecture, batch size, and task.

title: Important: Training Mode vs Evaluation Mode
text:
Important: Training Mode vs Evaluation Mode
BatchNorm
• Training: uses current mini-batch statistics.
• Evaluation: uses running statistics.
LayerNorm, GroupNorm, InstanceNorm
• Usually do not depend on other samples in the batch.
• Behavior is typically more stable for small batches.
Takeaway
BatchNorm requires extra care during validation and deployment.

title: PyTorch: Validation Discipline

PyTorch: Validation Discipline
Correct validation pattern
model.eval ()
with
torch.no_grad ():
y = model(x)
Why?
• model.eval() switches BatchNorm to running statistics.
• torch.no grad() disables gradient tracking.
Takeaway
For BatchNorm models, forgetting model.eval() can change validation
results.

title: Summary: Normalization Layers
text:
Summary: Normalization Layers
What normalization does
• Re-centers and re-scales activations.
• Preserves tensor shape.
• Adds learnable affine parameters in many settings.
• Improves optimization stability in many architectures.
Final insight
Normalization layers differ mainly by the axes used to compute mean and
variance.

title: Final Comparison
text:
Final Comparison
Memory rule
• BatchNorm2d: normalize each channel using batch and spatial statistics.
• InstanceNorm2d: normalize each sample-channel map independently.
• LayerNorm: normalize selected feature dimensions within each sample.
• GroupNorm: normalize groups of channels within each sample.
Practical rule
If batch size is large, BatchNorm is a strong CNN default. If batch size is
small, consider GroupNorm or LayerNorm.
